summary: Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Acharya Nagarjuna University under J. Sitaramamma (attested 2014) and studied under multiple traditional teachers, including Sayadaw U Kundala and U Sajjanasāra.

Sibani Das Gupta is an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Dhaka and under Rajendra Chandra Hazra. She completed a doctorate at the University of Calcutta by 1954 under the supervision of Sushil Kumar De.

Sibaraj Chetry works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sibnath Sarma, D. K. Chakravarty, N. Sharma, Girish Sarma, and M. Boruah, and was a Lecturer of Philosophy at North Lakhimpur College (attested 2012).

Sibnath Sarma is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He held a post at the Research and Archaeological Department in Jammu and Kashmir and served as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Gauhati University (attested 1999–2012).

Sicheng Liang (1901–1972) was an archaeology and history scholar. He studied at Tsinghua University (c. 1915–1923) and the University of Pennsylvania School of Design (c. 1924–1927), later holding a post at Peking University.

Sidney Lee (1859–1926) was educated at the City of London School (c. 1872–1878) and Balliol College, Oxford (c. 1878–1882). He later held an academic appointment at Queen Mary University of London from around 1913 to 1924.

Siegfried Goldschmidt (1844–1884) was an Indologist and linguist. He earned a Ph.D. at the University of Tübingen in 1867, studied under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth, and became an assistant professor at the University of Strasbourg in 1881.

Siegfried Lienhard (1924–2011) was an Indologist who earned degrees at Vienna (Dr. phil., 1949) and Stockholm (Habilitation, c. 1963). He was professor of Indology at Kiel University (1962–1968) and professor at Stockholm University (1968–1990).

Sieglinde Dietz (b. 1944) specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her PhD under Michael Hahn at the University of Bonn in 1980 and held a post at the University of Göttingen (attested 1990).
Signe Cohen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied under Ludo Rocher and serves as a professor at the University of Missouri.

Signe Howell (1942–2025) was a scholar in religious studies. She studied at SOAS (c. 1973–1976) and the University of Oxford (c. 1976–1980), and was appointed professor at the University of Oslo in 1989.

Silvia Luraghi (b. 1958) is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Turin (c. 1977–1982). She held posts at Turin (c. 1992–1998), Università degli Studi Roma Tre (c. 1996–1998), and the University of Pavia (c. 1998).

Silvio Vita (1954–2023) worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Naples "L'Orientale" and Princeton, taught at "L'Orientale" (1992–2001) and Sapienza (2006–2012), and directed the Italian School of East Asian Studies (c. 2001–2023).

Simo Parpola (b. 1943) is an Assyriologist and linguist who earned his PhD from the University of Helsinki in 1968. He served as associate professor at Chicago (1977–1979) and professor at Helsinki beginning in 1978.

Simon Cubelic is an Indologist affiliated with the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2018) and Documenta Nepalica (attested 2018), and is a professor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Simon P. James is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Durham University as a Tutor in the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and as a Lecturer in Philosophy (attested 2013–2014).
Simon Winant is an Indologist and linguist who is a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University (attested 2026).
Singhathon Narāsabho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at Visva-Bharati University under the supervision of Sudhindra Chandra Chakravarti.

Siniruddha Dash is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Director at the University of Madras (2000–2014), the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library (attested 2013), and the K. V. Sarma Research Foundation (2020).

Siran Upendra Deraniyagala (1942–2021) was an archaeologist who studied under Frank Raymond Allchin at Cambridge, and also at London and Harvard. He was Director General of the Department of Archaeology, Sri Lanka (c. 1992–2001).
